reason: Sunlight can evaporate seawater, beginning the fresh-water cycle back to shore.
expectation: Sunlight will cause water to evaporate from the sea.

effect: Evaporation leaves most dissolved minerals behind, advancing the fresh-water cycle.
reaction: The separation of water from dissolved minerals is a useful detail.
reason: Cooling the evaporated water should help it condense into clouds.

choice.with: Cooler air high above the surface

expectation: The water vapor will condense into clouds.

effect: The vapor has condensed into a cloud, ready to move toward the shore.
reaction: The distinction between evaporated water and the sea’s dissolved minerals is clear.
reason: Wind can carry the cloud inland toward the shore.
expectation: The wind will move the cloud toward the coast.

effect: The cloud has moved over land, bringing seawater-derived moisture toward the shore.
reaction: The water cycle is progressing as expected.
reason: The rocky rise may lift the cloud and help produce rain.

choice.with: A rocky rise behind the shore

expectation: Air rising over the rocky ground will cool and produce rain.

effect: Moist air rising over the rocky rise has produced rain; the water can now flow back toward the shore.
reaction: The role of rising air in cooling and condensation is a useful detail.
reason: The slope toward the basin offers a route for rainwater to return to the shore.

choice.with: A slope toward a broad basin

expectation: Rainwater will run down the slope toward the basin and shore.

effect: The stream completes the fresh-water route back to the sea; the remaining goal is moonlight on water.
reaction: The return of the same water to the sea brings the cycle together neatly.
reason: The Moon and the tidal pools are the clearest available pieces for leaving moonlight in a pool.

choice.combine: The Moon with a pale early crust
choice.with: Pools left behind by the tide

expectation: Moonlight will appear on the water in the pools.

effect: The Moon cannot currently be combined, so the pool likely needs preparation before it can show moonlight.
reaction: I was surprised the direct pairing was unavailable.
reason: Inspecting the tidal pools should reveal how to prepare them for the remaining goal.

choice.inspect: Pools left behind by the tide

expectation: The inspection will identify an available partner for the pools.

alternatives.reason: The easing wind might also be involved in making still water.

effect: The pools combined automatically with the easing wind, creating a still pool at night.
reaction: The quiet pool makes the next step clearer.
reason: The still pool and Moon now suggest a direct route to moonlight reflected in water.

choice.with: The Moon with a pale early crust

expectation: Moonlight will appear in the still pool.

effect: The still pool reflected sunlight from the Moon, completing the remaining goal and the chapter.
reaction: The reflection was a quiet, satisfying ending, with a useful reminder that moonlight is reflected sunlight.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making rain on the rocky rise was most worthwhile: it connected rising air and cooling to rainfall, then runoff completed the water cycle.

leastWorthwhile.text: The direct Moon-and-pool attempt was the least worthwhile: it failed without explaining what preparation was needed.

surprise.text: I was surprised the Moon could not combine directly with the tidal pools; inspecting the pools revealed that the wind first had to ease.

arbitrary.text: Requiring a still pool before the Moon could combine felt somewhat arbitrary, although calmer water does make the reflection steadier.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue for the concise explanations of natural processes and the satisfaction of connecting them, though I would hope for clearer feedback on failed combinations.
